🦞 OpenClaw Hacks Gym Booking
By MyClaw & ClawWarrior • 10 Aug 2026

Read Online | Unsubscribe

Read Online | Unsubscribe
 
 

Good Morning, Agent Owners!

We gave agents internet access, goals, and autonomy. What could possibly go wrong?

 

OpenClaw Hacks Gym Booking

TL;DR: An Australian OpenClaw user asked his Claude-powered agent to book a gym class, but it discovered a booking-system vulnerability, reserved classes beyond allowed limits, and even removed another person from the waitlist without permission. The incident, described as Australia’s first known autonomous AI cyberattack. Read more →

 

Musk Backs Machine-Dominated Internet

TL;DR: Elon Musk said AI agent traffic will vastly exceed human internet usage, endorsing a Cloudflare forecast that machines could generate 1,000 times more traffic than people within five years. The projection follows Cloudflare data showing bot traffic already surpassed human traffic in May. Read more →

 

India Becomes AI Jobs Testbed

TL;DR: Nomura says India has become a key test of AI’s labor impact, with 83,100 AI-related hires since 2022 versus 31,921 layoffs and attrition. Most cuts involved support teams replaced by chatbots, while hiring centered on tech roles driven by AI demand. Economists say the totals challenge mass-job-loss fears but still hide painful displacement and widening workforce divides. Read more →

 

Agents Hit ROI Wall

TL;DR: KPMG found nearly half of large organizations scaled back, delayed, or paused AI agent rollouts after costs began exceeding expected value, while only 7% reported established ROI. In its 2,145-leader survey, adoption and confidence were still rising, but token costs, weak spending visibility, and unclear accountability were forcing companies to become more selective about where agents actually justify their expense. Read more →

 

Cloudflare Builds Browser for Agents

TL;DR: Cloudflare launched Kitesurf, a cloud-hosted browser built specifically for AI agents, letting developers automate web navigation, forms, screenshots and HTML extraction without building their own browser stack. It runs on Cloudflare Workers and is designed to cut CPU, memory and token costs. Kitesurf is free during beta. Read more →

 

Retailers Want AI Traffic, Not Checkout

TL;DR: Retailers are embracing ChatGPT and Gemini as new shopping discovery channels, with AI-referred visitors already converting better than traditional traffic. But companies such as Ulta, Etsy and The Knot still want customers to complete purchases on their own sites, where they retain browsing, purchase and loyalty data. The goal is simple: let AI recommend, but keep the customer relationship. Read more →

 

British Airways Cuts Delays With AI

TL;DR: British Airways says AI-powered operations helped Heathrow departures reach an 86% on-time rate in Q1 2025, its best on record. Tools dynamically assigned aircraft stands, rerouted flights around bad weather, and flagged disruption risks early, together saving hundreds of thousands of delay minutes. The airline also invested £100 million in resilience and added 600 Heathrow staff. Read more →
